conviction_note: No vinstvarning and no numeric guide, so the whole quarter is new and JM's own report days move a median ~7% (Finwire: -12.0, +4.5, -2.4, -11.6, -9.4, -1.3, -10.2, -1.8). Inference from JM's own documents points to Q3 revenue and EBIT below the Modular consensus of 2,544 / 90.7: Q3 is seasonally 0.70-0.84x Q2 on revenue, no investor-project sale was announced in the quarter, and the drag from low-margin repurchased units is still there. Against that, Stockholm tenant-owned prices rose through September, the short is crowded at 11.66%, and the stock ran up 8% in five sessions. That gives p_up 44 on abs 7.0, so -0.84 scaled. The findings sum to -1.0 because they are each small inferences. The two numbers agree in sign and nearly in size.

findings.finding: JM announced no sale of a rental or investor project in Q3 2026: the Nasdaq Nordic feed has no 'JM selling residential project' item between the Q2 report (2026-07-10) and 2026-10-20. Q3 2025 had a 205-unit, SEK 687m sale to CapMan (announced 2025-07-04) and 236 investor units in total, and Q2 2026 had 186 investor units. So Q3 units sold and EBIT have none of the completion catch-up an investor sale brings and rest on consumer sales alone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 EBIT 59 against a consensus of 131 and revenue 2,137 against 2,684: the stock fell 11.6% on the report day (Finwire). The 2025 rental sale did not save that quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The units-sold consensus of 517, against 562 a year earlier, suggests analysts left out investor sales. The EBIT and revenue consensus of 90.7 / 2,544, up 54% and 19% y/y, does not look like it removed the investor-sale catch-up from the y/y base. If it had, the consensus EBIT would sit below Q2's underlying ~95 by more than seasonality explains.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 report: sold to investors 31 + 205 units in Q3 2025, https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a0cc47ff5f8f4650e9619e8a672a9ccc9

findings.finding: JM's own quarterly overview shows Q3 revenue at 0.70x Q2 in 2024 (2,515 vs 3,583) and 0.84x in 2025 (2,137 vs 2,540). Applied to Q2 2026 revenue of 2,815, that gives 1,970-2,365, while consensus 2,544 implies 0.90x. Analysts also missed Q3 2025 revenue by 20% (2,684 expected) and EBIT by 55%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Report days with an EBIT miss: Q3 2025 -11.6%, Q2 2026 -12.0% (70 vs 114). The Q1 2026 beat gave +4.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is fresh: all 6 contributors updated, and SEB and DNB Carnegie cut targets on 2 and 8 October. Even so, the revenue bar sits above both prior Q3/Q2 ratios. More units in production (5,116 vs 4,557) and a higher sold share (64% vs 51%) are a real reason for a higher ratio, which is why this stays small. A market that had absorbed the seasonal gap would not have bid the stock up 9.5% from 109.7 to 120.0 between 9 and 16 October.

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 report says the margin drag came from sales in projects with a low completion rate and from 'a large share of sales of residential units recognized in the balance sheet with a lower margin', plus about SEK 25m of one-offs. JM Stockholm's revaluation effect was -12 in Q2 2026 and -45 in Q3 2025, and 234 lower-margin repurchased units were still on the balance sheet. The CEO only promises margin improvement 'over time'. Consensus 3.54% equals Q2's underlying ~3.4% (95/2,815), so it assumes no seasonal dip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin is the line the Q2 2026 (-12.0%) and Q3 2025 (-11.6%) reactions turned on.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus EBIT of 90.7 is already below Q2's underlying 95. What is left is the seasonal margin dip, which consensus does not show; Q3 2025's margin of 2.8% was below Q2 2025's 4.6%.
findings.independence: none (same company document family as the second finding, but a different line: margin rather than revenue)

findings.finding: Svensk Mäklarstatistik's September release, published 8 October, shows Stor-Stockholm tenant-owned prices +2.0% m/m, rises on a 12-month basis in every region (central Stockholm ~+9%), and apartment sales volume +10% y/y. JM is Stockholm-weighted, and rising prices feed its percentage-of-completion revaluation effects, the line that was negative for JM Stockholm in Q2 2026 and Q3 2025.

findings.finding: JM's Q3 start releases total 295 units, all in JM Stockholm, against a starts consensus of 558. The share of starts JM announces has varied: 71% in Q3 2025 (211 of 296), 58% in Q2 2026 (392 of 679), 36% in Q1 2026 (155 of 425). So the implied actual is 415-820 and does not settle the line. JM has also said it 'still intend[s] to start production on more residential units in 2026 than in the previous year' (2,270 in 2025), which needs about 1,166 in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Starts are a secondary line. Q3 2025 starts of 296 (vs 637) came on a -11.6% day dominated by the EBIT miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts have the same releases. The coverage ratio of announcements is unstable, so this is a weak inference and sized near zero.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative and cut against the baseline's +3.41 priced lean (mostly the crowded-short squeeze term) and the +8.1% five-day run-up. The run-up lifts the bar further, while the crowded short is why p_up is held at 44 and not lower.
language_note: The Modular consensus table with all six KPIs, and Finwire's list of report-day reactions (-12.0, +4.5, -2.4, -11.6, -9.4, -1.3, -10.2, -1.8), came from the Swedish press (Placera/Finwire). The baseline's reaction history was a cadence estimate with a median of 3.31%; the Finwire list puts JM's actual report-day median near 7%, and that set abs_move_pct.
The September housing data (Svensk Mäklarstatistik), the Q3 2025 consensus-miss details (Börsvärlden) and the DNB Carnegie and SEB target cuts were only in Swedish-language sources.
JM's own filings are bilingual and carried nothing extra in Swedish. The Q3 report invitation exists only in Swedish, but its content (08:00 release) is routine.
lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat': the two main negatives agree with a crowded 11.66% short, so they were shrunk (-0.8 to -0.6 and -1.0 to -0.7) and p_up moved from 42 to 44
'A narrow proxy loses / macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the Mäklarstatistik finding was cut from +0.6 to +0.4
'Too small about the move': abs_move_pct was kept at 7.0, sized on the Finwire report-day distribution and not the baseline's 3.31 proxy; no pre-release means the numbers are new
print_vs_bar_pct moved from -12 to -10 to match the smaller inference-based negatives
